question_en: (1) The offer shows a 4,000 EUR security deposit but also a 1,000 EUR refundable deposit with 400 EUR non-refundable deductible with the mandatory Damage Waiver. Which applies to our booking? (2) What is the exact cost of the Damage Waiver? (3) With the Damage Waiver, is our maximum liability the 400 EUR, or could there be extra charges? (4) If we take independent deposit insurance (Yacht-Pool or other), is the 4,000 EUR deposit still required at check-in?
answer_exact: For our charters, we offer two different options. Option A – Independent Deposit Insurance & Refundable Security Deposit: You have the option to insure the full amount of the security deposit through an independent insurance company, such as YachtPool, Hamburg, Fairwinds, or another provider of your choice. The insurance must be arranged before your arrival. In this case, the standard refundable security deposit of €4,000 would still be withheld at check-in. This amount is fully refundable at the end of the charter, provided that there are no damages or other applicable charges. Option B – Damage Waiver on Arrival: If you arrive without independent deposit insurance, you may instead purchase our Damage Waiver through YachtPool upon arrival. For the Bali 4.2, this option consists of: €400 non-refundable Damage Waiver fee and €1,000 refundable security deposit. Therefore, by choosing the Damage Waiver, your maximum financial liability in relation to the security deposit would be reduced to €1,400 (€400 non-refundable fee + €1,000 refundable deposit), rather than the standard €4,000 security deposit. The €1,000 refundable amount is held against potential damages and is returned at the end of the charter, provided there are no applicable charges. The choice between the two options is entirely yours.

question_en: How do clause 9 and clause 3(b) work together? If a previously undetectable technical defect causes a major engine failure with no fault by us, could we be charged beyond the deposit?
answer_exact: The provisions you refer to should be read together. In general, when the yacht is under the Charterer's responsibility (as he is also the skipper), any expenses relating to damage or failure which is caused by his use of the yacht, and which is not attributable to normal and natural wear, are his responsibility. At the same time, our yachts are insured against the risks specified in our Terms & Conditions. Therefore, the Charterer is relieved from liability for losses or damages covered by the relevant insurance, provided that these have not been caused or contributed to by gross negligence or wilful misconduct. In practical terms, for a Skipper who arrives with independent charter insurance, the maximum amount for which the Skipper remains financially liable in relation to the yacht is generally the applicable security deposit. This amount is pre-authorised upon arrival and remains blocked for the duration of the charter. The exact amount depends on the type of yacht selected. Therefore, even in the event that a damage were to exceed the amount of the security deposit, the Skipper's liability in relation to the yacht would remain limited to the applicable security deposit, subject to the exclusions and conditions provided for in the Charter Agreement and the applicable insurance arrangements. I would also like to add that we are boat owners and we manage their maintenance and winterisation through our own private yard and technical team. We maintain service records for our yachts and have a detailed overview of their technical condition and maintenance history. Consequently, in a situation such as the one described in your example, namely a previously undetectable technical defect resulting in a major engine failure, without any fault or misuse by the Charterer or crew, this would not normally be treated as the Skipper's responsibility or charged to the Skipper.

question_en: Please clarify the wording on injuries on board in clause 3(b), including liability insurance protection for skipper and crew and its coverage limit.
answer_exact: Where the Charterer is also acting as the skipper, we would recommend that he has appropriate independent skipper insurance in place before the start of the charter. Such insurance should provide appropriate protection for the yacht and her equipment against fire, marine and collision risks, as well as third-party liability and losses or damages exceeding the applicable security deposit, in accordance with the specific terms and limits of the insurance policy. The exact coverage and applicable limits are therefore determined by the insurance policy and the security deposit applicable to the yacht selected for the charter.

question_en: Under clauses 4(a) and 16, how are delays caused by an unavoidable technical failure or an unforeseen official sailing prohibition treated?
answer_exact: Regarding the reference to an unforeseen official sailing prohibition, I would first like to clarify what type of situation you have in mind, so that we can provide you with an accurate answer. As we operate sailing yachts, a general unforeseen prohibition of sailing would not normally be applicable in the way it might be for certain other types of vessels, as the yacht is capable of sailing under sail. Could you kindly clarify whether by "delay" you mean: a delay during the charter which affects the planned duration or itinerary due to a possible technical failure; or a delay in returning the yacht to our base, for example due to adverse weather or other circumstances beyond the Charterer's control? Once we understand the specific situation you have in mind, we will be happy to clarify how it would be handled under the relevant clauses of the Charter Agreement. Should you be interested, we would also be delighted to prepare a quotation for your preferred charter. In this case, we would simply need to know: the week you would like to charter; the total number of guests; and whether you are interested in a monohull or a catamaran.

question_en: How do clause 9 and clause 3(b) work together? If a previously undetectable technical defect causes a major engine failure without our fault, could we be charged beyond the deposit?
answer_exact: In general, when the yacht is under the Charterer's responsibility (as he is also the skipper), any expenses relating to damage or failure which is caused by his use of the yacht, and which is not attributable to normal and natural wear, are his responsibility. At the same time, our yachts are insured against the risks specified in our Terms & Conditions. Therefore, the Charterer is relieved from liability for losses or damages covered by the relevant insurance, provided that these have not been caused or contributed to by gross negligence or wilful misconduct. In practical terms, for a Skipper who arrives with independent charter insurance, the maximum amount for which the Skipper remains financially liable in relation to the yacht is generally the applicable security deposit. This amount is pre-authorised upon arrival and remains blocked for the duration of the charter. The exact amount depends on the type of yacht selected. Therefore, even in the event that a damage were to exceed the amount of the security deposit, the Skipper's liability in relation to the yacht would remain limited to the applicable security deposit, subject to the exclusions and conditions provided for in the Charter Agreement and the applicable insurance arrangements. I would also like to add that we are boat owners and we manage their maintenance and winterisation through our own private yard and technical team. We maintain service records for our yachts and have a detailed overview of their technical condition and maintenance history. Consequently, in a situation such as the one described in your example, namely a previously undetectable technical defect resulting in a major engine failure, without any fault or misuse by the Charterer or crew, this would not normally be treated as the Skipper's responsibility or charged to the Skipper.

question_en: What does clause 3(b) say about injuries on board, including liability insurance protection for skipper and crew and its coverage limit?
answer_exact: Where the Charterer is also acting as the skipper, we would recommend that he has appropriate independent skipper insurance in place before the start of the charter. Such insurance should provide appropriate protection for the yacht and her equipment against fire, marine and collision risks, as well as third-party liability and losses or damages exceeding the applicable security deposit, in accordance with the specific terms and limits of the insurance policy. The exact coverage and applicable limits are therefore determined by the insurance policy and the security deposit applicable to the yacht selected for the charter.

question_en: Under clauses 4(a) and 16, how are delays from an unavoidable technical failure or an unforeseen official sailing prohibition treated?
answer_exact: Regarding the reference to an unforeseen official sailing prohibition, I would first like to clarify what type of situation you have in mind, so that we can provide you with an accurate answer. As we operate sailing yachts, a general unforeseen prohibition of sailing would not normally be applicable in the way it might be for certain other types of vessels, as the yacht is capable of sailing under sail. Could you kindly clarify whether by "delay" you mean: a delay during the charter which affects the planned duration or itinerary due to a possible technical failure; or a delay in returning the yacht to our base, for example due to adverse weather or other circumstances beyond the Charterer's control? Once we understand the specific situation you have in mind, we will be happy to clarify how it would be handled under the relevant clauses of the Charter Agreement. question_en: The offer shows a 4,000 EUR security deposit and also a damage waiver with 1,000 EUR refundable deposit and 400 EUR non-refundable. Which applies? What does the waiver cost? answer_exact: For our charters, we offer two different options: Option A - Independent Deposit Insurance & Refundable Security Deposit. You have the option to insure the full amount of the security deposit through an independent insurance company, such as YachtPool, Hamburg, Fairwinds, or another provider of your choice. The insurance must be arranged before your arrival. In this case, the standard refundable security deposit of 4,000 EUR would still be withheld at check-in. This amount is fully refundable at the end of the charter, provided that there are no damages or other applicable charges. Option B - Damage Waiver on Arrival. If you arrive without independent deposit insurance, you may instead purchase our Damage Waiver through YachtPool upon arrival. For the Bali 4.2, this option consists of: 400 EUR non-refundable Damage Waiver fee, 1,000 EUR refundable security deposit. Therefore, by choosing the Damage Waiver, your maximum financial liability in relation to the security deposit would be reduced to 1,400 EUR (400 EUR non-refundable fee + 1,000 EUR refundable deposit), rather than the standard 4,000 EUR security deposit. The 1,000 EUR refundable amount is held against potential damages and is returned at the end of the charter, provided there are no applicable charges. Any applicable charges would therefore be deducted from this amount in accordance with the terms of the Damage Waiver. The choice between the two options is entirely yours, depending on which arrangement you prefer.

question_en: Client of Big Orange Boat (skippered charter 2027): our T&C look written for a bareboat charterer and do not reflect the skipper's duties and liability.
answer_exact: You have booked a boat with a skipper, as clearly stated in the booking confirmation document, the very first document you received. The official document that the port authorities require so as to stamp the boat's documents require the skipper's certificate and their details as the master of the boat. The charter party agreement and the terms you have modified cannot be changed at this stage, as the section regarding the skipper's liability must be signed by him. At the end of the document, it is explicitly stated that both the charterer (you) and the skipper are required to sign the contract. Since this agreement is designed to outline the responsibilities of both parties, you, as the charterer, are accountable for your part, while the skipper is responsible for the terms you requested to modify. To move forward, I recommend preparing a supplementary document to reassure you of the skipper's liability and presence. In general, as guests on board, you bear no responsibility for the boat's sailing capability.

question_en: (Standard block in offer emails) How does the security deposit work?
answer_exact:
OPTION A: Independent Deposit Insurance & Refundable security deposit. You have the option to secure full coverage for your security deposit by purchasing insurance from an independent insurance company. The insurance must be completed BEFORE arrival. You can insure your deposit through Yachtpool, Hamburg, Fairwinds or any other insurance company. The refundable amount based on yacht's specification is normally withheld on spot.

OPTION B: Damage Waiver (On-Arrival Option). If you arrive without independent insurance, the only available option is to purchase a Damage Waiver through YachtPool, which includes: a non-refundable fee (calculated based on the yacht's specifications) and a refundable deposit that is held in case of damage. You retain the option to insure the refundable portion on the spot.

question_en: What does a fully crewed charter include regarding fuel, provisions and port fees (implied by request for total pricing)?
answer_exact: Please note that fully crewed charters require an APA (Advanced Provisioning Allowance). This is an advance payment that covers operating expenses such as fuel, provisions, onboard supplies, and port and marina fees. The crew manages these expenses on your behalf, keeping track of all costs and providing receipts. Any remaining balance is refunded to you at the end of your trip. This arrangement allows you to enjoy your holiday with greater flexibility and without having to handle individual expenses along the way.

answer_exact: Please allow me to explain the two security deposit options available. The first option is the Damage Waiver, which reduces the security deposit from €4,000 to €1,000. This option consists of two separate amounts: €400 non-refundable fee: This amount is paid directly to the insurance company through a QR code that we will provide upon your arrival at our office during the check-in and paperwork procedure. €1,000 refundable security deposit: This amount is secured through a credit/debit card pre-authorization. Provided that the yacht is returned and there are no damages or outstanding charges at the end of the charter, the pre-authorization will be released. Second Option (Security Deposit Insurance): If you want to proceed with the standard 4,000 EUR pre-authorization, then you will need to make an independent charter insurance by using one of the independent companies that are out there such as Yachtpool, Hamburg, Fairwinds or any other insurance company. If you have independent insurance, you can proceed with the pre-authorization of the full amount. Our requirement is only regarding the security deposit. Regarding travel insurance, please note that there is no specific requirement or restriction on our part. Arranging travel insurance is entirely optional and at your discretion. Our website simply provides general information about travel insurance that you may find useful if you wish to explore this option. Attached you will also find the charter party we have sent to Mr. [client].

question_en: What are your payment and cancellation conditions?
answer_exact: Our payment terms are as follows: 50% of the total charter fee is due within seven days of booking confirmation to secure the reservation. The remaining 50% is due 56 days before embarkation. Our cancellation policy applies to the total charter fee as follows: 120 days or more before embarkation: The advance payment will be refunded in full. Fewer than 120 days before embarkation: The company will retain the amount paid, subject to our Rebooking Guarantee (Credit Policy). Rebooking Guarantee (Credit Policy): If the cancelled yacht is successfully rebooked by another client under exactly the same terms, including the charter period, price and conditions, the amount paid will be converted into credit towards a future charter with us. The credit must be used for a new charter commencing no later than 30 October of the following year. Credits are non-transferable and cannot be redeemed for cash.

question_en: What are your payment and cancellation conditions?

For a bareboat skipper with independent charter insurance, the maximum amount the skipper is generally financially liable for in relation to the yacht is the applicable security deposit. Our yachts are insured against the risks listed in our Terms & Conditions. The charterer is relieved from liability for losses covered by that insurance unless caused by gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

A previously undetectable technical defect, such as a major engine failure without fault or misuse by the charterer, would not normally be charged to the skipper. We own the boats, maintain them and winterise them in our own private yard with our own technical team, and keep service records.

When the charterer is also the skipper we recommend independent skipper insurance before the charter, covering the yacht against fire, marine and collision risks, third-party liability and losses above the security deposit.
